episodes.177110: Following the recent events which produced widespread flooding across the central California Interior, another atmospheric river plunged through the region on March 14 and 15 producing heavy precipitation, flooding and strong winds with several stations measuring gusts exceeding 60 mph. Much of the Sierra Nevada picked up another 3 to 6 inches of liquid precipitation with snow levels above 8500 feet while the adjacent foothills picked up 2 to 4 inches of rainfall while the San Joaquin Valley and West Side Hills generally picked up between 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rainfall.
episodes.177137: Another in a series of AR events brought valley rain, mountain snow, and high winds. Due to the valley rain, some snowmelt occurred leading to localized flooding.
episodes.178160: A strong atmospheric river produced widespread moderate to heavy rainfall across Southern California March 14-15. Rain amounts of 1 to 3 inches were observed across the coastal basin, with heavier amounts up to 4 inches reported in the mountains. Rain fell on an extremely deep snowpack in the mountains, resulting in flooding. Flooding also occurred across the coast and valleys, where several debris flows occurred.
episodes.178172: Strong low pressure meandered just off the southeast coast of New England from late on the 13th to early on the 15th, before moving eastward and farther offshore.  In its wake, it produced 2 to 3+ feet in northern and western MA.  Lesser amounts of 6-12 were common over interior lower elevations.  In eastern CT, RI and eastern MA, a coating to 2 inches were common, as precipitation type was mainly wet snow and rain.  The storm did produce onshore wind gusts up to 50 kt over the eastern MA waters.
episodes.178359: Higher than normal moisture content combined with a southeasterly wind flow produced showers and thunderstorms from the streamer that developed from the El Yunque area into the San Juan metro area. The Doppler radar estimated between 2 and 5 inches of rain in and around Carolina, Hato Rey, and San Juan, where flooding was reported.
episodes.178551: A wet system brought periods of heavy rain with flooding. There was 1 to 2 feet of snow accumulated above 6,500 feet, locally higher on some peaks. Heavy rain fell bringing widespread roadway flooding, as well as local mudslides, flash flooding, with evacuations ordered in some areas. Thunderstorms with large hail, strong damaging winds and tornadoes were reported. Strong winds gusting to 55 to 75 mph brought down numerous trees and powerlines across the area, causing widespread and extended power outages.
episodes.178627: A trough of low pressure moving eastward across California brought a plume of deep moisture to Arizona as well. The synoptic-scale ascent from the trough combined with the moisture allowed for periods of heavy rain over Arizona March 15 and 16.  Surface dewpoints were similar to summer time...in the 40s and 50s. The heavy rainfall, high snow levels, and deep snow pack combined to produce rapid snow melt and significant runoff into area waterways.
episodes.178737: Another winter storm brought gusty winds and accumulating snow to much of Utah in the middle of March. Precipitation combined with snowmelt also resulted in flooding, mostly in southern Utah, including noted fatalities in a popular slot canyon.
episodes.178974: Another atmospheric river pounded the Desert Southwest, bringing flooding and strong to severe thunderstorms to northwest Arizona.
episodes.178975: Another atmospheric river pounded California with heavy snow, flooding rains, and strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.178976: Another atmospheric river pounded the Desert Southwest, bringing heavy mountain snow and lower elevation flooding to southern Nevada.
episodes.179198: A strong low pressure system moved through the region bringing widespread strong winds and heavy rain to southeast Oregon.
episodes.192577: Another system in an active period resulted in periods of moderate to heavy rainfall across southern Utah, resulting in isolated flash flooding.

events.narrative: Broadcast media reported mandatory evacuation orders for the commercial trailer park called Loveys Landing due to flooding near the Sacramento River.
The California Highway Patrol reported water rushing across the roadway at Whitmore Road and Cow Creek Road.
California Highway Patrol reported flooding on Hornitos Rd. at Slate Gulch Rd. and Indian Gulch Rd.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding at Dersch Road and Hyrax Road.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across the Inland Empire from the evening on March 14 through the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 2.00-3.50 fell, with local amounts up to 4 inches closer to the San Bernardino County Mountains. Flash flooding was reported early on the morning of March 15; firefighters responded to a vehicle in swift moving water, and the rescue was successful. Also, Grove Ave between Merrill Ave, Chino and Riverside Ave in Ontario saw 2 to 4 inches of running water covering the entire roadway. Kimball Ave in Chino between Quality Way and Euclid Ave were flooded with 2 to 4 inches of standing water.

events.narrative: At 12:10 am on 3/15/23, buoy 44018 reported a wind gust to 58 mph.
Warm temperatures, rainfall, and snowmelt caused flooding of SR278, and a minor mudslide at mile marker (MM77). SR278 was reduced to 1 lane.
Warm temperatures, rainfall, and snowmelt caused flooding of SR278, and a minor mudslide at mile marker (MM75). SR278 was reduced to 1 lane.
The ASOS station at the Ontario airport measured 0.75 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station RTFO3 16 miles east of Riversside measured 0.73 inches of heavy rain.
The agrimet station ONTO 3.8 miles southwest of Ontario measured 0.75 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station FCKO3 16.0 miles east southeast of Frenchglen measured 1.50 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station FGFO3 1.1 miles southwest of Frenchglen measured 0.66 inches of heavy rain.
The ASOS station at Burns airport measured 0.74 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station LMCO3 measured 1.11 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station RLYO3 measured 1.22 inches of heavy rain.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across inland Orange County from the evening on March 14 through the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 1.50-2.50 fell. An MPing report of street and road flooding resulting in road closures and stranded vehicles was reported near Santa Ana early in the morning on March 15.
California Highway Patrol reported a rockslide at the intersection of SR 178 and Democrat Rd.

Significant flooding was reported early in the morning on March 15 by the Department of Highways.||SR-78 near Carlsbad initially saw flooding around 3 AM on March 15, with flooding starting on the on-ramp, eventually expanding onto the eastbound lanes of SR-78, and into the westbound lanes nearly two hours later. A hard closure was announced around 5:30 AM for the eastbound lanes, with the westbound lanes closing around 7 AM.||Flooding was reported on Discovery St near San Pablo Ct, with a closure reported on Discovery St around 8 AM.||La Costa Ave was flooded at El Camino Real.||Widespread rainfall of 2.00-3.00 was reported in the 24 hours surrounding the flooding in coastal north county.

Mudslides, rockslides and debris flows were reported across western portions of the San Bernardino County Mountains on March 15 as widespread heavy rainfall of 1.00-3.50+ inches occurred. Rockslides occurred along the upper passing lanes on SR-330 near Running Springs; mud and rocks blocked the upbound lanes of Highway 18 at Old Waterman Canyon Road near Crestline; rocks were reported across the road on SR-18 near Crestline, and a vehicle reportedly hit the rocks.

Flooding occurred early in the morning on March 15 following very heavy rainfall over the previous 24 hours, with precipitation amounts of 2.5-3.5 inches. Huffstalter St between 5th and 2nd St was closed due to flooding, as well as Pala Temecula Road.
The Department of Highways reported a rockslide on the southbound lanes of SR-76 early in the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 2.50-3.50 inches occurred with the event.
UDOT reported a debris flow / mudslide over US-191 near MP 262, resulting in road closure for cleanup.

Flooding occurred near Big Bear City on March 15 following heavy rainfall of 0.50-1.50, with reports of 2.00-3.00+ inches nearby. Heavy rain combined with snow melt to lead to flooding in the San Bernardino County Mountains. The Department of Highways reported the closure of Gildart Drive and Division Drive; Irvine Way and Barrett Way were flooded; the riverbed broke through and resulted in flooding at SR-38, with 3 inches of standing water reported between Baldwin and State Lane.

Oak Creek began flooding in Oak Creek Canyon around 700 AM on March 15.  The road was closed near Orchard Canyon Lodge and Banjo Bill Campground. There was 3 feet of water above the road at a stage of 5.22 feet at the Sedona gauge. Cooper Cliffs Road was closed by 1100 AM MST due to the flooding. Doodlebug and New Castle Lane were close at around 200 AM on March 16. The creek remained above this level for just over 3 days. The peak flow as about 10.5 feet at 800 AM MST on March 16.||The Oak Creek gauge near Cornville (OACA3) showed more than a 7.5-foot rise from             5.2 feet at 1PM March 15 to a crest of 12.76 feet at 115 AM on March 16. The gauge dropped back to around 5.2 feet by 1000 AM March 17. ||The Sedona Police Department reported that evacuations were made along Oak Creek from the evening of March 15 through the morning of March 16.  The locations that were evacuated include Rancho Sedona RV Park,  Trails End Road, Trails End Lane, Blackhawk Lane, Newcastle Lane, Oak Creek Mobilelodge,  Sycamore Road, The Center of the New Age, and the Villas at Poco Diablo Resort. ||A rock slide closed Highway 89 through the upper part of Oak Creek Canyon (switchbacks) about 3 miles north of Slide Rock State Park around 323 PM on March 16.

Law enforcement reported flooding in addition to video showing that Ash Creek was flowing outside of bankfull levels. An additional photo showed Ash Creek at the top of Blackridge at exit 36 was underwater.
The Granite Creek Gauge showed water rising from 6.00 feet around 400 AM MST March 15 to a crest of 8.00 feet at midnight on March 16.
The Department of Highways reported a rock slide on both the upbound and downbound lanes on SR-38.
The Department of Highways reported a large boulder blocking the southbound lanes of Highway 78.
Highway 322 was damaged due to flooding of the Meadow Valley Wash. The road fully reopened in late May.
The Department of Highways reported at leas three big boulders blocking SR-74.
Hackberry Road was closed.
Water flowed over Spring Mountain Ranch Road.
Warm temperatures, rainfall, and snowmelt caused flooding of of Monte Neva Road near McGill, causing a section of road to be eroded through, the road has been closed.

Persistent moderate to at times heavy rain resulted in flash flooding throughout Beaver Dam Wash. For example, the Catclaw Canyon stream gage increased from a dry no-flow state of 0 CFS to a peak flow of approximately 2923 CFS. Cameras also showed water flowing in this typically dry wash.
Blake Ranch Road was closed from mile marker 15 to Highway 93.
Highway 317 was closed due to flooding of the Meadow Valley Wash.
Zion National Park reported multiple waterfalls and high flows at various locations throughout the park associated with ongoing rainfall.
Flooding reported at Amarillo and Buckwheat Road, with rain of 0.50 inch reported.
Hilldale Dispatch reported multiple low-lying road closures due to high flows on Short Creek.

A significant landslide occurred following heavy rain in San Clemente on the 1500 block of Buena Vista the morning of March 15. All buildings were immediately evacuated, with no injuries reported. At least four apartment buildings had been red-tagged by the afternoon (deemed too dangerous to enter).
Swiftwater rescue conducted by firefighters at Matthews Rd and Palomar Rd, with a vehicle submerged in one foot of water, with four occupants rescued.
Firefighters responded to a vehicle submerged in 1 foot of water at Matthews Road and Palomar Road. Four occupants were rescued from the vehicle.
Moderate rain in the higher elevations plus melting snow flooded Highway 159 in multiple places between Calico Basin Road and Blue Diamond Road.
Broadcast media reports Gene Autry Trail, North Indian Canyon Drive and Araby Drive in the Coachella Valley closed due to flooding.

The Verde River Gauge near Clarkdale started raising rapidly around 1000 AM March 15 from around 8.00 feet to a crest of around 15.8 feet by 1100 PM MST on March 15. The Verde River dropped back to around 8.0 feet by 900 AM on March 18.  The Verde River in Camp Verde started to rise rapidly around 500 PM on March 15 from 11.8 feet. The crest was at 20.8 feet at 300 March 16 and the river returned to 11.8 feet by 900 PM on March 19.  The Verde River below Tangle Creek began to rise rapidly around 500 PM from 12.0 feet.  The crest was around 700 PM at 20.3 feet and slowly fell back to 12.0 feet by 400 PM by 400 PM March 19.||Homes were flooded along Bates Drive in Cottonwood.
Hildale Street, Central Street, and Academy Avenue were closed due to rises on Short Creek.
Urban flooding was reported in Calle M in Hato Rey.
Flooding was reported on Simon Madera Avenue, near the intersection of the Ramal 8. A house and the street were affected by the flood waters.
Parking lot flooded near road 190 and Ave. Jose Tony Santana. The flood waters were reaching the floors of the cars.

Broad areas of sheet flooding were observed in the greater Tremonton area due to rain on snow. Roads in communities near the Sky Way Golf Course in Tremonton were noted to be under several inches of water, with several homes impacted. Water was also reported to be overflowing the banks of the Malad River and Bear River.

Extensive flooding was reported along Dry Beaver Creek across Kimberlys Way (150 feet wide). The river gauge upstream reported a 4 foot rise. The creek crested around midnight on March 16 at about 4.5 feet above the creek bed.

The Wet Beaver Creek gauge near Rimrock rose from 5.5 feet at 1000 AM MST on March 15 to 9.4 feet at 400 PM. The creek dropped back to 5.5 feet by noon on March 17. A local newspaper reported that areas along Wet Beaver Creek were evacuated.  This included Rimrock near Lake Montezuma and people along Beaver Vista Drive and Rimrock Drive.  An overnight shelter was set up at Camp Verde Middle School.
The West Clear Creek gauge near Camp Verde showed a 5-foot rise from 2.8 feet at noon on March 15 to a crest of 8.1 feet by 100 AM March 16. The water level returned to 2.8 feet by 9 AM on March 17.
The Department of Highways announced the closure of Highway 78 between Wynola Road and the Banner Store due to a mudslide in the eastbound lanes.
A public video showed flooding from the Virgin River at Man O War Road, with a bike trail underwater as a result.
Law enforcement reports and social media photos showed water flowing over South Old Highway 91 in New Harmony at Ashcreek Reservoir.
A family of 5 was hiking in Snow Canyon State Park and was stranded by a flooded wash due to the combination of precipitation and snowmelt. The family needed to be rescued via a swift water rescue.
Thunderstorm winds damaged carports, trees, and roofs.
Caltrans reported 2 feet of water (photos included) on fast lane of state highway 60 at Jack Rabbit Trail, causing lane closures.  Between 400 and 418 pm local.
Highway 95 was closed near 7th Street, and multiple swift water rescues were needed.
The J Street offramp of Interstate 40 East was flooded.
Needles Highway was flooded.
Amboy Road near Roy's was flooded.
